title: Checkpoint: Modern and Contemporary
objective: After this level you can explain the main movements in art since 1945.
summary: Since 1945 each movement answered the last: Pop, Minimalism, conceptual and land art. In 1968 critics called the trend the dematerialization of art.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: watch the artwork get lighter.
cards.body: Since the late 1940s, artists kept asking how little an artwork really needs. Here's the chapter in order, then how each move answered the last, and the name two critics gave the whole trend.

events.label: Pollock pours Autumn Rhythm on the floor
Hamilton's bodybuilder holds a POP lollipop
Warhol's 32 Soup Cans line a shelf
LeWitt: the idea makes the art
Spiral Jetty coils into Great Salt Lake

cards.headline: Each move answered the last
cards.body: Pop swapped Abstract Expressionism's personal feelings for impersonal, everyday images. Minimalism found Action painting too personal and cut art down to simple geometric shapes that refer to nothing but themselves. Conceptual art made the idea more important than the object, and land art, part of that wider movement, walked out of the gallery into the landscape.

cards.fact: In 1968, two critics named the trend: the dematerialization of art.
cards.context: Lucy Lippard and John Chandler described "ultra-conceptual" art, where the idea matters more than the object. Look back along the timeline: paint on canvas, printed images, factory bricks, written instructions, a rock spiral in a lake. At almost every step, the object got lighter and the idea got heavier.

mascot.line: If you remember one thing from this chapter: the object got lighter, the idea got heavier.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: How art since the 1940s got lighter and more about ideas, as each movement answered the last.
Why Pop artists like Warhol borrowed ads and comics, and repeated images like products.
What makes a row of bricks or a set of instructions into art, for Minimalists and conceptual artists.
Why a painting can sell for hundreds of millions: a rare name, a famous image and two bidders.

questions.prompt: What did Lippard and Chandler mean by the "dematerialization" of art?

options.label: Artworks were being stolen from museums
Art where the idea matters more than the object
Paintings fading as their pigments aged
options.rationale: It's about what art is made of, not decay.

options.label: Art made only by machines
options.rationale: Machines aren't the point; ideas are.

questions.explanation: Their 1968 essay described "ultra-conceptual" art in which the idea matters more than the object.

questions.prompt: Modern recap: which of these came first?

options.label: Warhol's Soup Cans
Pollock's Autumn Rhythm
LeWitt's essay on conceptual art
Smithson's Spiral Jetty

questions.explanation: Pollock painted Autumn Rhythm in 1950, years before the others.

questions.prompt: From Level 81: what did Harold Rosenberg say the canvas had become?

options.label: A window onto a landscape
options.rationale: That's the old idea of painting he left behind.

options.label: A mirror of the viewer
options.rationale: His metaphor was about the painter acting.

options.label: A page from a comic book
An arena in which to act

questions.explanation: Rosenberg called them action painters because the canvas became an arena in which to act.

questions.prompt: From Level 86: how did Ansel Adams change his Moonrise prints over the years?

options.label: He raised the contrast: whiter moon, darker sky
He added color by hand
He cropped the moon out
options.rationale: The moon is the star of the picture.

options.label: He softened the focus to look painterly

questions.explanation: Adams printed the negative many times, raising the contrast to whiten the moon and darken the sky.

questions.prompt: From Level 88: what happened to Girl with Balloon just after it sold in 2018?

options.label: It was stolen from the auction room
options.rationale: It stayed right there, partly shredded.

options.label: Banksy painted over it on stage
It partly shredded itself in its frame
It was sent back to the street wall
options.rationale: It became a new artwork instead.

questions.explanation: A shredder hidden in the frame cut it partway, and it became a new work, Love Is in the Bin.
